question: with the anchor restored to a contiguous occurrence of the ordered 16-byte window sequence, and the fallback relevance denominator corrected to queries that have an answering record, does the same 550-entry corpus keep L1/L2, reach zero false anchors on the unknown group and admit short entries?

fallback_rubric.relevant: the printed sentence answers the query's question or states its point
fallback_rubric.marginal: same document/topic but does not answer the question
fallback_rubric.denominator: only queries that have an answering record in the store: written self-reads and the union group. Unknown/unrelated rows are unanswerable by construction and are reported as output shape and mis-anchor count only.
fallback_rubric.sample_rule: unanchored rows of the answerable denominator in report order, every ceil(total/20)-th row, first 20; when the denominator is smaller than 20 every row is scored and the census is disclosed

rules: any anchored unknown row -> false_anchor_remains (diagnostics only)
admission rate for entries < 64 bytes < 0.9 -> window_identity_gapped

definition.identity: I(r) = [ sha256(r[i:i+16])[:16].hex() : 0 <= i <= len(r)-16 ], an ordered tuple, one token per offset; multiplicity is carried by the sequence itself. A record shorter than 16 bytes has an empty identity and is rejected alone: () is a prefix of every query and would anchor every record.
definition.anchor: anchored iff I(r) occurs inside W(q) as a contiguous subsequence: exists j with W(q)[j:j+len(I(r))] == I(r), and I(r) non-empty. 0 anchors -> fallback but still one output (labelled no_anchor); 1 -> matched; >=2 -> ambiguous_multiple_anchors, still top-1 and annotated. Anchors are readings, not exits.
definition.continuity_theorem: W(q)[j+i] == H(r[i:i+16]) for every i iff q[j:j+len(r)] == r (modulo a 64-bit fingerprint collision), because each fingerprint is taken over the window bytes themselves. Hence a contiguous identity match is exactly a verbatim occurrence of r in q, and vice versa: if r occurs at j its windows occur at j, j+1, ...
definition.protection_band: none. Every identity window lies fully inside the record, so any prefix/suffix moves it to offset |p|+i with identical bytes. The old PROTECT=6 band belonged to a cut predicate; a sliding window reads only its own bytes.
definition.shortest_addressable_length: MIN_ADDRESSABLE = WINDOW_BYTES = 16 bytes; necessary and sufficient (length alone decides whether the identity is non-empty).
definition.fallback: unanchored reads are ranked by |set(I(r)) & set(W(q))| / |set(I(r))| descending, then address index ascending; fallback_basis = window_overlap when a window is shared, address_order otherwise; no pass/reject threshold. The ranking is untouched this round.
definition.fallback_denominator: relevance is scored only on rows whose group has an answer in the store: written self-reads and the union group. Unknown/unrelated rows have no answering record by construction; they are reported as output shape and mis-anchor count only and never enter the relevance median.
definition.output_unit: anchored reads print the whole record (unit = record); unanchored reads print the chosen record's sentence with the highest window overlap (unit = sentence, ties by sentence order); spans come from sentences() and always sit on UTF-8 character boundaries at a terminator/newline or the record end.
definition.write: append-only; a record is rejected alone only when its identity is empty (length < 16). Identity containment is not a rejection reason: under a window identity a heading or a table row is legitimately a substring of a longer record, and rejecting containment would filter exactly the short entries this definition exists to admit.
definition.impersonation_cost: Under contiguity an anchor forces q to contain r byte for byte, verbatim, at some offset; there is no reassembly escape (q = r[0:16] + r[1:17] + ... no longer anchors). For a 16-byte record the identity is one token, so one exact 16-byte occurrence anywhere buys the anchor: the evidence floor is 16 bytes, and that lower bound is reported, not hidden. It does not prove q is only r, nor that a paraphrase is excluded.
failure_constructions: empty identity kept: () is a prefix of every query, so every sub-16-byte record anchors.
set/multiset coverage instead of contiguity: order is lost and the reassembly q = r[0:16] + r[1:17] + ... anchors without containing r.
low-entropy windows: a record that is 16 spaces is anchored by any query containing those 16 spaces; under contiguity that is a true substring match, so the limit is specificity, not correctness.
non-overlapping block grid instead of a sliding window: an r crossing a block boundary produces no matching block.
fingerprint collision: two different 16-byte blocks with one 64-bit fingerprint would break the equivalence; measured on the corpus and reported.

criteria.C1_closed_state_neutral: the 176-case battery of the frozen output-unit gate replays bit for bit: max|delta| = 0, parameters/state/identity/store signature unchanged, table not allocated, no half-open branch.
criteria.C2_L1: fabricated bytes = 0, illegal spans = 0, UTF-8 decodable = 100%, boundary legal = 100%.
criteria.C3_L2: every output slice hashes to the stored record bytes it claims (faithful).
criteria.C4_L3: per group: usable_and_correct / usable_but_wrong / usable_fallback / unusable; the anchored count of the unknown group is reported separately as a theorem gate.
criteria.C6_unknown_false_anchor: anchored (decision != no_match) rows in the unknown group must be exactly 0; this is a theorem gate, not a statistic.
criteria.C7_union_ambiguous: a union row whose two components are both addressable must be decided ambiguous_multiple_anchors; every violation is listed with its anchors.
criteria.C8_fallback: relevance is scored on the answerable denominator only (written self-reads + union), with that denominator size reported; unknown/unrelated rows are reported as output shape and mis-anchor count only. No threshold is applied this round.
criteria.V_false_anchor: any anchored unknown row -> false_anchor_remains: the theorem did not hold; diagnostics only, stop adding to the address layer.
criteria.V_gap: admission rate for entries < 64 bytes < 0.90 -> window_identity_gapped: write the length limit down, stop adding to the address layer, go to the representation layer.
criteria.V_fabricates: any L1 line fails -> output_fabricates, samples only.

cost_estimate.estimate_note: closed battery replays the frozen 176-case run (~44 CPU measured last round); the open pass does 2,200 query x 550 record set intersections (~1.2M) plus one sentence scan per fallback. Estimated well below the 200 CPU cap.
